status: Working result. Fresh local scoped review; formal acceptance and commit pending.

scope.preparation: Fixed round radius and held reference depth of the smooth-well one-increment geometry, same coherent monopole of action 1 and aligned real dipole. A static hold may balance a mean carrier load. One fixed-current axisymmetric OpenSleeve with a rigid reflecting side, one entrance and open receiver on a half-length core supplies the stationary number current (archived constituent mass is 1). The steady solve and the reduced bend dynamics are separate models. There is no time-dependent angular carrier solve or magnitude of its traction in these results. For an isotropic background a linear dipolar perturbation integrates to zero change of the scalar total current by angular orthogonality, while allowing a finite dipole force. Higher-order intake changes are unmeasured.
scope.linear_hypothesis: State (q,qdot,b,bdot): qddot+omega_d^2 q+g cos(omega_s t)b=0; M bddot+C bdot+K b+g cos(omega_s t)q=F(t). M=12, K=6, C=.1 or 6.5. g=0.618498902707 sqrt(2/omega_s) from the archived profile. The axial profile f(w)=sin^2(2pi w/L) on |w|<L/2 is multiplied by cos(theta); b is the signed displacement at unit profile. pde.tex equations linpde-wall-action and linpde-harmonic-modes admit effective inertia, axial and angular stiffness and a material forcing. They do not identify either tested C for the prepared flowing well. The model treats the support as a maintained coherent pump. The reported low/high drive is a single force on that wall coordinate with a specified phase. Subtraction of a static load cannot calibrate dissipative traction.
scope.drive_and_fit: Single-tone steady solutions use a periodically forced linear evolution, demodulation and a switch-off of the external force. Observed displacement is the Fourier component at the driven tone. The other frequency components remain in the generator. The wall signal sampled once each support period yields the four roots of a rank-four linear prediction; 72- versus 180-sample fits and half-strength inputs agree. Reported energy rates describe the envelope of the dipole-dominated mode. The bend has an additional mechanical pole pair; the full time trace is not a single exponential. Units of time, length, generalized force and scalar amplitude are those of the archived toy model.
scope.phase_locked_test: At the exact frequencies omega_d ± omega_s and absent direct dipole loss, the undriven Fourier equation at omega_d enforces b_- + b_+ = 0. Reciprocity of the symmetric harmonic stiffness for the real cosine pump makes both diagonal responses equal and the conversion response opposite to them. Equal in-phase forces give 2 F cos(omega_s t)cos(omega_d t); the steady solution b=0 and q=(2F/g)cos(omega_d t) satisfies both equations. At release from the common maximum the net bend acceleration is -2F/M. The numerical pair starts from rest and propagates the forced period map using repeated squaring to periodic settling, then measures the free wall signal with the support pump still on. Detuning, direct dipole damping and other couplings can lift the cancellation. Its presence alone cannot determine bend damping.
scope.lines: A conditional three-level line readout assigns the carrier action increment 0.03. The widths use one Markov jump sqrt(Gamma)a at zero bath temperature and no pure dephasing. Select 01 and 12 coherences separately, give each equal integrated area, and add their signals. Their decay rates are Gamma/2 and 3Gamma/2 (FWHM Gamma and 3Gamma); feeding of 01 by 12 does not enter a selective 12 measurement. Assume the common shift of the tracked dipole pole for both transitions. Using the archived printed additions introduces only roundoff against the stored conservative angular splitting. The independently checked extrema are for this ideal spectral test. Neither the full quantum response under pump nor the actual readout of a passing parcel has been measured.
scope.next: At matched intake prescribe this angular wall motion and extract the generalized force from the time-dependent carrier, using its density and stress at the wall, with outgoing boundary conditions, matched no-drive subtraction, and power at support and inlet separated. For a single Fourier component the passive loss per cycle after this subtraction constrains the dissipative part of the bend impedance. Independently test intrinsic wave loss, coherence noise and both line shifts. The present comparison adds neither a mirror-odd electric source nor a net moving-mouth free-fall force.

"""Independent finite-sideband reduction, complex quadratic pencil, and exact stationary-point count."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import numpy as np
from numpy.polynomial import Polynomial

archive = json.loads(Path("research/pde_ledger_v3/_measurements/mouth_trapped_wave_spectrum.json").read_text())["runs"]


def read(run, prefix):
    line, = [s for s in archive[run]["stdout_lines"] if s.startswith(prefix)]
    return {k: float(v) for k,v in (s.split("=") for s in line.split()[1:] if "=" in s) if "," not in v}


point = read("smooth_dipole_l015_01","point n=1 ")
bow = read("mouth_wave_linewidth_budget01","bow h=0.015 ")
levels = read("smooth_dipole_l015_01","levels ")
wd, ws = point["omega_d"], point["omega_s"]
g = bow["overlap"]*np.sqrt(2/ws)
gap = (levels["relaxed_first"]-levels["relaxed_second"])/.03
for c in (.1,6.5):
    for N in (5,9,15):
        n = np.arange(-N,N+1)
        is_wall = (n % 2) == 1
        mass = np.where(is_wall,12.,1.)
        drag = np.where(is_wall,c,0.)
        stiff = np.where(is_wall,6.,wd**2)
        coupling = np.diag(np.full(len(n)-1,g/2),1)
        coupling += coupling.T.copy()
        at = [N-1,N+1]
        def dynamic(z):
            freq = z+n*ws
            return coupling + np.diag(stiff-mass*freq**2+1j*drag*freq)
        def response(z):
            return np.linalg.solve(dynamic(z), np.eye(len(n))[:,at])[at,:]
        exact = response(wd)
        rounded = [response(bow["difference"]+ws)[0,0],response(bow["sum"]-ws)[1,1]]
        b1 = (1j*drag-2*mass*n*ws)/mass
        b0 = dynamic(0)/mass[:,None]
        companion = np.block([[np.zeros_like(b0), np.eye(len(n))],[b0,np.diag(b1)]])
        roots = np.linalg.eigvals(companion)
        root = roots[np.argmin(abs(roots-wd))]
        gamma = 2*root.imag
        print(f"C={c:g} N={N} exact_abs={abs(exact[0,0]):.13g} lag={-np.angle(exact[0,0],deg=True):.13g} diff_response={abs(exact[1,1]-exact[0,0]):.3g} opposite_cross={abs(exact[0,1]+exact[0,0]):.3g} rounded_abs={abs(rounded[0]):.13g},{abs(rounded[1]):.13g} rounded_lag={-np.angle(rounded[0],deg=True):.13g},{-np.angle(rounded[1],deg=True):.13g} pole={root.real:.13g} energy_rate={gamma:.13g}")
    # x relative to broad-line center in units of gamma. Common shift cancels.
    broad = Polynomial([0,1])
    narrow = Polynomial([-gap/gamma,1])
    # The positive denominators are cleared in the exact derivative.
    stationary = 1.5*broad*(narrow**2 + .25)**2 + .5*narrow*(broad**2+2.25)**2
    extrema = sorted(z.real for z in stationary.roots() if abs(z.imag)<1e-10)
    print(f"C={c:g} dimensionless_spacing={gap/gamma:.12g} real_extrema={extrema} maxima={(len(extrema)+1)//2}")
